clue.text: Be prepared to make an investment

definitions.note: an investment here is a siege, investing a town by surrounding it

parts.note: prepared means set, as in ready to go

explanation.surface: A financial adviser tells a client to get ready before putting money into something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Investment' looks financial, but to invest a fortress is to besiege it, which is what beset means.
explanation.definitionFit: To besiege or surround a place is the old military sense of investing it.

clue.text: Where air travellers buy cheap pails?

definitions.text: Where air travellers buy cheap pails?

parts.words: Where air travellers buy cheap pails?
parts.note: a discount ticket agency, read literally as a store selling buckets

explanation.surface: A shop where flyers pick up budget buckets.
explanation.definitionFit: An outlet for discounted airline tickets has a slang name that literally suggests a pail shop.

clue.text: Dash into view during a gun-fight

definitions.meaning: to rush out suddenly into sight

explanation.surface: Someone runs out in the middle of a gunfight.
explanation.definitionFit: To dart out is to burst forth, and a gun battle is a decisive duel with firearms.

clue.text: The highest score excellent is excellent

parts.note: top means the highest
a notch is a scored mark, a nick cut in a surface

explanation.surface: Getting the top mark is a fine thing.
explanation.walkthrough: A score here is a cut mark, not a tally of points.
explanation.definitionFit: First-rate and of the highest quality, as the best of something is.

clue.text: Leading position for security-firm driver

definitions.meaning: the foremost part of an advancing army or movement
read as two words, a guard who rides in a security company's van

explanation.surface: A job advert offering a top spot as a driver for a security company.
explanation.definitionFit: The front rank of an advance is its forefront, and split in two the word names a guard on an armoured van.

clue.text: Endorsement is needed to enter Virginia

indicators.note: entering means the word is goes inside the abbreviation

parts.note: VA is the abbreviation for the US state of Virginia

explanation.surface: Travellers need a stamp in their passport to get into the American state.
explanation.definitionFit: A visa is a stamp of approval on a passport, endorsing entry.

clue.text: Hollow circle found in a wood

indicators.note: found in means the circle sits inside the wood

parts.note: a grove is a small wood
O is the shape of a circle

explanation.surface: A ring-shaped dip discovered in a forest.
explanation.definitionFit: A channel or furrow is a hollow cut into a surface.

clue.text: A drama produced by the navy

indicators.note: a drama that is produced is staged afresh, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A play put on by the fleet.
explanation.definitionFit: A fleet of warships, famously the Spanish one of 1588, is a navy.

clue.text: Arranged to be taken for a ride!

definitions.meaning: settled or agreed, as in a deal

explanation.surface: Something fixed up so that someone gets conned.
explanation.definitionFit: A deal that is settled is concluded, and a victim who is conned has been cheated.

clue.text: Woodcutters need false teeth

definitions.meaning: people or tools that chop timber

explanation.surface: Lumberjacks apparently require dentures.
explanation.definitionFit: Axemen chop wood, and slang calls dentures by the same name for their biting work.

clue.text: Recommend taking small case into a meeting

indicators.note: the short case is put inside the letters for a meeting

parts.note: a date is an arranged meeting
voc. is the short form of vocative, a grammatical case

explanation.surface: Someone suggests bringing a little briefcase along to a meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small case' sounds like luggage, but it is the abbreviation for the vocative case in grammar.
explanation.definitionFit: To advocate a course is to speak in favour of it, urging others to adopt it.

clue.text: Brilliant material from Italian poet around one past midnight

indicators.note: around means the poet's name goes round the other letters

parts.note: Dante is the Italian poet of the Divine Comedy
I is the Roman numeral for one
am marks hours after midnight

explanation.surface: Sparkling fabric from an Italian poet, after one in the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: Diamante is fabric or decoration covered in glittering paste gems.

clue.text: Competitors without work exhibit loss of energy

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the competitors surround the work

parts.note: the entry for a race is the field of competitors
op is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: Contestants with no job show signs of flagging.
explanation.definitionFit: In physics this is the measure of disorder, often glossed as energy becoming unavailable for work.

clue.text: Roy ought to make it with milk

definitions.text: Roy ought to make it with milk

indicators.note: to make suggests the letters of Roy ought are formed into something new

explanation.surface: Roy should prepare a dairy product using milk.
explanation.definitionFit: Yoghurt is cultured from milk, which is what Roy is told to do.

clue.text: Generally one should admit a grave error

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so the word one takes the jumbled letters inside
an error suggests the letters of a grave are wrongly ordered

explanation.surface: A general remark that anyone ought to own up to a serious mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' gives its own letters as the container, not the digit 1; 'should admit' tells it to take the shuffled letters inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking things as a rule, in the typical case, is the same as saying usually.

clue.text: British capitalists conclude during Paschal Sunday

indicators.note: during means the word for conclude falls inside the festival

parts.note: Paschal means of Easter
to end is to conclude

explanation.surface: British financiers wrap up business over the Easter weekend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capitalists' means residents of the capital: East Enders live in London's East End.
explanation.definitionFit: Londoners from the eastern district are inhabitants of the British capital.

clue.text: Browbeat so as to feature in the news

definitions.meaning: read whimsically as striking the lines on one's forehead
to appear prominently in newspaper reports

explanation.surface: Bullying someone in order to get into the papers.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is cryptic: a brow is a head, and beating it is hitting the head's lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Making front-page news is getting big headlines, while the playful reading has forehead wrinkles being struck.

clue.text: Member with a liking for the letter of the law

definitions.text: for the letter of the law
definitions.note: describes a person, a stickler who is all for strict legal wording

parts.note: a leg is a limb or member
list is an old word for desire or liking

explanation.surface: An MP who loves the exact wording of legislation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member' looks parliamentary but it is a limb.
explanation.definitionFit: A stickler for rules adheres strictly to legal wording over spirit.

clue.text: A subject of importance at Aintree

definitions.meaning: Aintree racecourse hosts the Grand ..., Britain's most famous steeplechase

explanation.surface: Something significant at the racecourse.
explanation.walkthrough: Aintree, near Liverpool, is home to the Grand National, a famous British horse race.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of a state is one of its people, and the big Aintree steeplechase is called the Grand one.

clue.text: Equal value put on a horse of the first order

parts.note: par means equal value, as in shares trading at par
a mount is a horse for riding

explanation.surface: A punter backs a horse at even money, hoping it is top class.
explanation.definitionFit: Something supreme or of chief importance is foremost and pre-eminent.

clue.text: How to shoot through that's the problem

definitions.meaning: to pierce with many holes, as with bullets

explanation.surface: A Hamlet-style musing on gunfire.
explanation.definitionFit: Peppering with shot leaves holes, and a puzzling question is a conundrum.

clue.text: Mean business

definitions.meaning: an affair or subject in hand

explanation.definitionFit: To be of importance is to count, and an affair in hand is a concern.

clue.text: Euphoria causes family member to lose his head

indicators.note: losing a head means the first letter of the relative is dropped

parts.note: a relation is a member of one's family

explanation.surface: A relative becomes so excited he loses control.
explanation.definitionFit: Intense joy and high spirits are what this feeling of euphoria amounts to.

clue.text: Consider putting Tory leader in to arbitrate

indicators.note: putting a letter in means it is inserted inside the word for arbitrate

parts.note: to mediate is to arbitrate between parties

indicators.note: the leader of Tory is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Thinking about bringing in the Conservative party chief to settle a dispute.
explanation.definitionFit: To ponder or reflect at length on something is to contemplate it.

clue.text: A Frenchman gets first-rate staff

parts.note: M is the abbreviation of monsieur, a French title
ace means first-rate

explanation.surface: A Frenchman acquires an excellent workforce.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceremonial club or rod of office carried in procession is a kind of staff.

clue.text: Take a sea voyage partly to relax

indicators.note: partly means only part of these words is used

explanation.surface: Go on a cruise to unwind.
explanation.definitionFit: To lessen tension or let up is to slacken, making things less strained.

clue.text: Everyone arranges a nice marriage

parts.note: all means everyone

indicators.note: arranging puts the letters of a nice into a new order

explanation.surface: The whole family sets up a pleasant wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: A union by marriage, especially between families, is a classic kind of alliance.

clue.text: Curse former City business charge

parts.note: ex means former
EC is the postcode area of the City of London
a business rate is a local tax charged on commercial property

explanation.surface: A grumble about the old financial district's business tax.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district, postcode EC; business rates are a British property tax on firms.
explanation.definitionFit: To execrate is to denounce or call down evil on, which is to damn.

clue.text: They take money made from labours on the land

explanation.surface: Money earned from farming.
explanation.definitionFit: Cash drawers collect payments, and a farmer working the soil cultivates it.
